title: Laminar Flow Hood (Clean Bench)

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

purpose: Provides a HEPA-filtered, particulate-free airflow across a work surface to protect the product/sample from environmental contamination — distinct from a biological safety cabinet, which is designed primarily to protect the operator and environment from the sample.
operatingPrinciple: Room air is drawn through a HEPA filter and directed in a smooth, unidirectional (laminar) stream — either horizontally or vertically, depending on the unit — across the work area, sweeping airborne particulates away from the work surface before the operator can introduce them near an open sample or plate.
basicOperation: Allow the blower to run for the manufacturer-specified warm-up period before beginning work, to establish stable laminar airflow.
Disinfect the work surface before and after use.
Avoid placing items, or your arms/hands more than necessary, in a way that disrupts the laminar airflow pattern over the work area.
Keep only the materials needed for the current task inside the hood to minimize airflow disruption and contamination risk.
importantSettings: Airflow direction (horizontal vs. vertical, fixed by the specific unit's design)
calibration: Periodic professional certification of HEPA filter integrity and airflow velocity per facility schedule.
maintenance: Do not block the front or rear air intake/exhaust grilles.
Report any unusual noise, vibration, or airflow alarm to facility maintenance rather than continuing to use the unit.

commonErrors.cause: Confusing a laminar flow hood (product protection only) with a biosafety cabinet (also protects the operator and environment) and using it for material requiring operator/environmental containment
commonErrors.fix: Use a laminar flow hood only for product-protection tasks with material that poses no meaningful hazard to the operator; use a certified BSC for anything requiring containment

safety: A laminar flow hood does NOT protect the operator from the sample — never use it for work with pathogens or hazardous biological material that requires containment; use a biological safety cabinet instead.
Do not disrupt airflow with rapid arm movements or by placing large equipment that blocks the airflow path.
